t_categories.title: The three FME categories
t_categories.why: This is the opening question in almost every FME interview. It shows whether you understand the licensing spine of GIFT IFSC fund management — everything else hangs off which category the FME holds.
t_categories.explanation: Under the IFSCA (Fund Management) Regulations, 2025, a fund manager in IFSC registers as one of three categories of Fund Management Entity (FME): Authorised FME, Registered FME (Non-Retail), and Registered FME (Retail). The category decides who you can raise money from, what schemes you can run and what activities you may undertake. Each higher category can also do everything the lower ones can.
t_categories.practicalPoint: In practice the category is chosen up front based on the business plan — retail vs accredited/private-placement money, and whether the firm wants PMS, REIT/InvIT or ETF activity. You cannot quietly switch category later; a change needs prior IFSCA approval.
t_categories.example: A boutique setting up a single venture capital scheme for a handful of accredited investors would register as an Authorised FME. A firm running restricted schemes plus portfolio management would take Registered FME (Non-Retail). A house planning public retail schemes or ETFs needs Registered FME (Retail).
takeaway: Authorised FME → VCS / Single Family Investment Fund (private placement)
Registered FME (Non-Retail) → restricted schemes + PMS + private REIT/InvIT
Registered FME (Retail) → retail schemes, public REIT/InvIT, ETFs
Higher category = superset of the lower ones
Category change needs prior IFSCA approval

t_networth.title: Net worth requirements
t_networth.why: A clean thresholds question. Interviewers use it to check that you actually know the numbers, not just the concepts.
t_networth.explanation: The minimum net worth is tied to the FME category: Authorised FME USD 75,000; Registered FME (Non-Retail) USD 500,000; Registered FME (Retail) USD 1,000,000. It must be maintained at all times, not just at registration.
t_networth.practicalPoint: A branch can maintain net worth at the parent level, but the parent must ensure funds for the branch's day-to-day operations. This net worth is separate from, and in addition to, net worth needed for any other regulated activity the group runs.
takeaway: Authorised — USD 75,000
Non-Retail — USD 500,000
Retail — USD 1,000,000
'At all times', not just at entry
Separate from other-activity net worth

t_kmp.title: KMP structure of an FME
t_kmp.why: Tests whether you understand the governance backbone — who must be appointed, and when a firm needs more than a Principal Officer.
t_kmp.explanation: Every FME must designate a Principal Officer responsible for the overall activities of the FME — fund management, risk management and compliance. A Registered FME must additionally appoint one KMP as Compliance Officer. A Registered FME (Retail) must also appoint an additional KMP for fund management before filing its first retail scheme or ETF offer document. Any FME managing AUM of at least USD 1 billion (excluding fund-of-funds AUM) must appoint an additional fund-management KMP within six months of the financial year end.
t_kmp.practicalPoint: All these KMPs must be based out of the IFSC. The structure scales with the business: a small Authorised FME may run on a Principal Officer alone; a large retail house will carry a PO, a Compliance Officer and separate fund-management KMPs.
takeaway: Every FME → Principal Officer
Registered FME → + Compliance Officer
Registered FME (Retail) → + fund-management KMP
AUM ≥ USD 1bn (ex-FoF) → + fund-management KMP
All KMPs based in IFSC

t_thresholds.title: Investor & corpus thresholds
t_thresholds.why: Cross-checks that you can separate 'who can invest' from 'how big the fund must be' — a common area where candidates blur the numbers.
t_thresholds.explanation: Restricted schemes are for accredited investors or investors putting in at least USD 150,000, and are capped at 1,000 investors. The minimum corpus for a Venture Capital Scheme and for restricted schemes is USD 3 million; a VCS corpus must not exceed USD 200 million.
t_thresholds.practicalPoint: Accredited-investor status removes the minimum-ticket floor. Employees and directors of the FME investing in the scheme are subject to a lower minimum. Always state whether a number is an investor-eligibility threshold or a fund-size threshold.
takeaway: Restricted scheme investor floor — USD 150,000
Max 1,000 investors in a restricted scheme
VCS / restricted scheme min corpus — USD 3 million
VCS corpus cap — USD 200 million
Accredited investor = no minimum ticket

t_po_role.title: The Principal Officer's mandate
t_po_role.why: If you are interviewing for PO, this is the question. It tests whether you grasp the breadth of the accountability you would be taking on.
t_po_role.explanation: The Principal Officer is responsible for the overall activities of the FME — including, but not limited to, fund management, risk management and compliance. It is a single point of senior accountability across the firm, not a narrow function.
t_po_role.practicalPoint: In an interview, don't reduce the PO to 'the person who signs filings'. Frame it as ownership of the firm's regulatory posture: making sure the FME operates within its category, its KMP structure is intact, and issues are escalated and resolved.
takeaway: PO owns overall FME activities
Spans fund management, risk and compliance
Single senior accountability point
Must be based in IFSC
Not merely a filing signatory

t_kmp_eligibility.title: KMP eligibility — qualification & experience
t_kmp_eligibility.why: Interviewers check whether you know the actual eligibility bar — and the shortcuts that apply to a Compliance Officer.
t_kmp_eligibility.explanation: A KMP generally needs a professional qualification or a post-graduate degree/diploma (minimum one year) in finance, law, accountancy, business, commerce, economics, capital markets, banking, insurance or actuarial science — or a CFA/FRM — plus at least five years of related experience in an eligible institution. A Principal Officer with 15 years of fund-management experience can qualify on a graduate degree in any field.
t_kmp_eligibility.practicalPoint: For the Compliance Officer, the experience requirement drops to three years where the person holds a professional qualification. Professional qualification includes ICAI / ICSI / ICMAI membership — and for the Compliance Officer, an LLB also counts. This clause was substituted by the 2026 amendment, so quote it as the current position.
takeaway: Base: professional qual / PG degree + 5 yrs experience
PO with 15 yrs FM experience → graduate in any field
Compliance Officer → 3 yrs if professionally qualified
CA / CS / CMA count; LLB counts for CO
Amended w.e.f. 30 Jan 2026 — cite as current

t_fit_proper.title: Fit & proper — a continuing test
t_fit_proper.why: A judgement question dressed as a knowledge question. Interviewers want to see that you treat fit & proper as ongoing, not a one-time box.
t_fit_proper.explanation: The FME, its directors, KMPs and controlling shareholders must be fit and proper persons at all times. It covers integrity, competence, financial soundness and absence of relevant regulatory or criminal findings.
t_fit_proper.practicalPoint: The phrase that matters is 'at all times'. If a director is later found not fit and proper by a regulatory order, that has consequences for the FME — so monitoring the status of key persons is a live compliance task, not a registration formality.
takeaway: Applies to FME, directors, KMPs, controlling shareholders
'At all times' — continuing obligation
Covers integrity, competence, soundness, record
A later adverse order affects standing
Monitoring status is a live compliance task

t_po_vs_co.title: PO vs Compliance Officer
t_po_vs_co.why: A favourite distinction question. It separates candidates who memorised titles from those who understand the governance design.
t_po_vs_co.explanation: The Principal Officer owns the overall activities of the FME. The Compliance Officer — a mandatory additional KMP for a Registered FME — is specifically responsible for compliance with the regulations and for implementing risk-management policies and practices. The PO's remit is broad; the CO's is focused on the compliance and risk function.
t_po_vs_co.practicalPoint: An Authorised FME may not have a separate Compliance Officer at all — the PO carries compliance. So the right answer depends on the FME category. Say that, and you show you understand the structure rather than a slogan.
takeaway: PO = overall activities of the FME
CO = compliance + risk implementation
CO is mandatory for a Registered FME
Authorised FME may run on PO alone
Answer depends on FME category

t_ppm_vs_offer.title: Placement memorandum vs offer document
t_ppm_vs_offer.why: The core documentation distinction. For a Legal & Compliance role this is fundamental — mixing up the two signals you don't understand private vs public fund raising.
t_ppm_vs_offer.explanation: A placement memorandum (the PPM) is the document by which an FME invites accredited investors — it belongs to private placement. An offer document is how a Registered FME (Retail) invites the public. The right document follows the FME category and the type of scheme.
t_ppm_vs_offer.practicalPoint: The PPM is the investor's primary disclosure document: strategy, risks, fees, conflicts, terms. Getting disclosure right in the PPM is where most of the legal-and-compliance work sits for non-retail funds.
takeaway: PPM = private placement, accredited investors
Offer document = public, Retail FME
Document follows category and scheme type
PPM is the investor's primary disclosure
Disclosure quality is the core L&C job

t_ppm_filing.title: Filing & 'taken on record'
t_ppm_filing.why: Tests process literacy — whether you know a PPM is filed and taken on record, not 'approved' in the retail sense.
t_ppm_filing.explanation: For restricted / VCS schemes the FME files the placement memorandum with IFSCA along with the fee; the scheme proceeds once the memorandum is taken on record, and the FME must incorporate any changes IFSCA communicates. A memorandum has a validity window within which the FME must reach first close.
t_ppm_filing.practicalPoint: Language matters in interviews: say the PPM is 'taken on record' for private schemes rather than 'approved'. Note that failing to reach minimum corpus within the window has consequences, including options to extend on paying part of a fresh filing fee.
t_ppm_filing.verifyNote: Exact validity periods and fee percentages vary by scheme chapter — confirm the specific numbers against the relevant chapter before quoting them.
takeaway: PPM filed with IFSCA + fee
Scheme proceeds once 'taken on record'
Incorporate IFSCA's communicated changes
First close within the validity window
Say 'taken on record', not 'approved'

t_pmla_po.title: FME Principal Officer vs PMLA Principal Officer
t_pmla_po.why: One of the most common trap questions in a compliance interview. Two very different roles share the same title.
t_pmla_po.explanation: The Principal Officer under the FME regulations owns the overall activities of the FME. The Principal Officer under the PMLA framework is the officer responsible for furnishing information — such as suspicious transaction reports — to FIU-IND. The PMLA framework also requires a Designated Director, who bears senior responsibility for the reporting entity's AML compliance.
t_pmla_po.practicalPoint: They can be different people. In an interview, name both roles, say what each is responsible for, and note that the Designated Director sits at senior-management level while the PMLA Principal Officer is the operational reporting point.
t_pmla_po.verifyNote: SAMPLE CONTENT — VERIFY AGAINST SOURCE. The uploaded PMLA file is a scanned image; confirm exact definitions and duties against the PMLA and PML Rules text.
takeaway: FME PO → overall FME activities (FM Regs)
PMLA PO → reporting to FIU-IND (STRs etc.)
Designated Director → senior AML responsibility
They can be different individuals
Don't collapse the two roles

t_cdd_edd.title: CDD, EDD and beneficial ownership
t_cdd_edd.why: Bread-and-butter for a Compliance Officer. Interviewers want to hear the logic: risk-based due diligence, and who you look through to.
t_cdd_edd.explanation: Customer Due Diligence means identifying and verifying the client and understanding the purpose of the relationship. Enhanced Due Diligence applies to higher-risk clients — for example PEPs or complex structures. Beneficial ownership means identifying the natural persons who ultimately own or control the client, not stopping at the immediate entity.
t_cdd_edd.practicalPoint: The point interviewers listen for is 'risk-based'. You don't apply the same intensity to everyone; you calibrate. And you always look through layers to the ultimate beneficial owner.
t_cdd_edd.verifyNote: SAMPLE CONTENT — VERIFY AGAINST SOURCE. Confirm BO thresholds and EDD triggers against current PML Rules and the applicable AML guidelines.
takeaway: CDD = identify + verify + understand purpose
EDD = extra scrutiny for higher-risk clients
BO = ultimate natural persons in control
Approach is risk-based, not uniform
Look through the structure

t_ifsc_fema.title: How IFSC sits within FEMA
t_ifsc_fema.why: For cross-border and legal roles, interviewers test whether you understand why GIFT IFSC is treated differently for exchange-control purposes.
t_ifsc_fema.explanation: An IFSC unit is, for many purposes, treated as a person resident outside India under the exchange-control framework, which is what lets GIFT IFSC operate as an offshore-in-onshore jurisdiction. Fund flows in and out, and downstream investment into India, run through this lens.
t_ifsc_fema.practicalPoint: Frame it as 'why the structure exists': the FEMA treatment is what allows an IFSC fund to raise and deploy foreign capital efficiently. Then flag round-tripping as the risk regulators watch — capital leaving India and returning dressed as foreign investment.
t_ifsc_fema.verifyNote: SAMPLE CONTENT — VERIFY AGAINST SOURCE. The uploaded FEMA file is a scanned image; confirm the precise resident/non-resident treatment and any current notifications before quoting specifics.
takeaway: IFSC unit ≈ non-resident for many FEMA purposes
Enables offshore-in-onshore fund structures
Inflows / outflows / downstream run through FEMA
Round-tripping is the watched risk
Explain the 'why', flag the risk

t_valuation_custodian.title: Valuation & the independent custodian
t_valuation_custodian.why: Tests the ongoing-obligations side of the job — the things that keep a fund compliant after launch.
t_valuation_custodian.explanation: An FME must appoint an independent custodian, generally based in IFSC, for the securities it manages. Valuation must follow the prescribed norms; for certain schemes a valuation report is prepared periodically (for example, a half-yearly report within one month of the period end).
t_valuation_custodian.practicalPoint: For a Compliance Officer this is calendar work: independence of the custodian and valuer, timeliness of valuation reports, and making sure reports aren't stale when relied upon.
t_valuation_custodian.verifyNote: Exact valuation frequencies differ by scheme type — confirm the specific frequency for the scheme in question.
takeaway: Independent custodian, generally IFSC-based
Custodian not mandatory for some FoF setups
Valuation follows prescribed norms
Reports on a defined cycle, filed on time
Independence + timeliness are the compliance points

t_reporting.title: Periodic & event-based reporting
t_reporting.why: Directly tests a Compliance Officer's core deliverable — knowing what's periodic, what's event-driven, and roughly when things are due.
t_reporting.explanation: Compliance splits into periodic reporting (regular investor and regulatory reporting on a set cycle) and event-based reporting (things triggered by a specific event — a change in KMP, a material change, a filing). Investor reporting for certain services runs at least quarterly, within a month of quarter end.
t_reporting.practicalPoint: In an interview, structure the answer as two buckets — periodic vs event-based — then give one concrete example of each. That structure alone signals that you'd run a real compliance calendar.
takeaway: Two buckets: periodic and event-based
Periodic runs on a fixed cycle
Event-based is triggered by a specific change
Some investor reporting is quarterly (+1 month)
A compliance calendar ties it together

t_reading_enforcement.title: How to read an enforcement action
t_reading_enforcement.why: Interviewers sometimes hand you a real order and ask 'what went wrong here?'. They're testing whether you can extract a lesson without over-reading the order.
t_reading_enforcement.explanation: Read any enforcement action in five moves: the facts, the specific provision breached, the deficiency the regulator identified, the consequence, and the lesson. Keep the lesson tied to what the order actually establishes.
t_reading_enforcement.practicalPoint: The discipline is not to inflate an order into a broad legal principle. Say what the FME did, which obligation it missed, and what control would have prevented it — nothing wider than the order supports.

case.title: Illustrative pattern (not a specific order)
case.facts: An FME onboarded investors before beneficial-ownership verification was complete.
case.issue: AML/KYC obligation not met before the relationship proceeded.
case.deficiency: Onboarding control allowed the file to advance with a gap.
case.consequence: Regulatory observation; remediation of the onboarding process.
case.lesson: Make BO verification a hard gate before onboarding can proceed.

t_reading_enforcement.verifyNote: SAMPLE CONTENT — VERIFY AGAINST SOURCE. This is an illustrative pattern, not a real order. Use only authoritative IFSCA orders in the live product.
takeaway: Facts → provision → deficiency → consequence → lesson
Tie the lesson to what the order establishes
Don't inflate an order into a legal principle
Always end on the control that prevents recurrence

questions.q: What are the different categories of FME under the current IFSCA framework?
questions.answer: Under the IFSCA Fund Management Regulations there are three categories of Fund Management Entity. An Authorised FME runs venture capital schemes or a single-family investment fund, raising from accredited investors by private placement. A Registered FME (Non-Retail) runs restricted schemes for accredited or above-threshold investors, and can also do portfolio management and private-placement REITs and InvITs. A Registered FME (Retail) can run retail schemes for the public, do public REITs and InvITs, and launch ETFs. Each higher category can also do everything the lower ones can.
questions.trap: Don't say there are 'AIF categories' — that's the domestic SEBI AIF vocabulary. In IFSC the licence is the FME category; scheme types sit under it.
questions.tip: Lead with 'there are three categories', then take them in order. Structure signals confidence.

questions.q: What is the difference between the Principal Officer and the Compliance Officer of an FME?
questions.answer: The Principal Officer is responsible for the overall activities of the FME — fund management, risk and compliance together. The Compliance Officer is a separate KMP, mandatory for a Registered FME, who is specifically responsible for compliance with the regulations and for implementing the firm's risk-management policies. So the PO's remit is broad and the CO's is focused. In a smaller Authorised FME there may be no separate Compliance Officer at all — the Principal Officer carries that too.
remember: Authorised FME may run on PO alone
questions.trap: Don't imply every FME must have a Compliance Officer. It depends on the FME category.
questions.tip: End by tying it to category — that's what separates a memorised answer from an understood one.

questions.q: Is the Principal Officer of an FME the same as the Principal Officer under the PMLA?
questions.answer: No — they share a title but they're different roles. The Principal Officer under the FME regulations owns the overall activities of the FME. The Principal Officer under the PMLA framework is the person responsible for furnishing information, like suspicious transaction reports, to FIU-IND. The PMLA framework also has a Designated Director at senior-management level for AML responsibility. The two Principal Officers can be different people, and you shouldn't treat them as one.
questions.trap: The whole question is the trap — candidates instinctively say 'yes, same person'. It isn't necessarily.
questions.tip: Answer 'no' clearly, then explain both. A confident distinction here is a strong signal.
questions.verifyNote: AML detail — verify against PMLA / PML Rules.

questions.q: What is a PPM and how is it different from an offer document?
questions.answer: A PPM — placement memorandum — is the document an FME uses to invite accredited investors into a private-placement scheme. An offer document is what a Registered FME (Retail) uses to invite the public. So the PPM is the private-placement disclosure document, and the offer document is the retail one. The PPM is the investor's main source of information on strategy, risks, fees and terms.
questions.trap: Don't call the PPM a 'prospectus' — that's retail/public language.
questions.tip: Anchor the difference on private vs public. Everything else follows.

questions.q: What are the net worth requirements for the three FME categories?
questions.answer: Net worth tracks the category: an Authorised FME needs USD 75,000, a Registered FME (Non-Retail) needs USD 500,000, and a Registered FME (Retail) needs USD 1,000,000. It has to be maintained at all times, and it's separate from any net worth needed for other regulated activities.
questions.trap: It's 'at all times', not just at registration — say that and you show you understand it as an ongoing obligation.
questions.tip: If you blank on a number, give the ranking — Authorised lowest, Retail highest — then the figures.

questions.q: What qualification and experience does a KMP of an FME need?
questions.answer: Broadly, a KMP needs a professional qualification or a post-graduate degree or diploma in a relevant field — finance, law, accountancy, business, economics and so on — or a CFA or FRM, plus around five years of related experience in an eligible institution. A Principal Officer with fifteen years of fund-management experience can qualify on a graduate degree in any field. For the Compliance Officer, the experience requirement is lower — three years where the person is professionally qualified.
remember: PO with 15 yrs FM → any graduate degree
questions.trap: The lower experience bar is specific to the Compliance Officer — don't apply it to every KMP.
questions.tip: Note it was amended in Jan 2026 — showing you track amendments is a plus.

questions.q: As Compliance Officer, the business team wants to push a transaction you think may breach a regulatory limit. How do you handle it?
questions.answer: First I'd establish the facts precisely — what exactly is proposed, the amounts, the counterparties. Then I'd identify the specific obligation or limit that's in play and assess how close we are to breaching it. If there's genuine regulatory risk, I don't just say no — I explain the issue to the business, look for a compliant way to achieve the commercial goal, and escalate to the Principal Officer where the call is significant. Whatever we decide, I document the rationale, and if the transaction can't proceed compliantly, it doesn't proceed.
questions.trap: Don't answer as either a pushover ('I'd let it go') or a blocker ('I'd just refuse'). Show structured judgement.
questions.tip: Say the framework out loud — facts, regulation, risk, escalation, action, documentation. It shows you think like a compliance professional.

questions.q: An FME registered as Authorised now wants to run restricted schemes. Can it just start?
questions.answer: No. Restricted schemes sit under the Registered FME (Non-Retail) category, so the firm would need to be in that category. An FME can't change its category on its own — that needs prior approval from IFSCA. So the practical answer is: apply to move category first, then run the restricted schemes.
questions.trap: Don't assume 'higher category can do lower activities' means you can drift upward freely — moving up needs approval.
questions.tip: Answer the yes/no first, then the 'because'. Interviewers like a clear position followed by the reason.

questions.q: One of the FME's directors is named in an adverse regulatory order. As Principal Officer, why should you care?
questions.answer: Because fit and proper is a continuing test — the FME, its directors, KMPs and controlling shareholders have to remain fit and proper at all times, not just at registration. An adverse order against a director can affect that standing and therefore the FME. So as Principal Officer I'd treat monitoring the status of key persons as a live compliance task, assess the impact of the order, and act on it rather than filing it away.
remember: Adverse order can affect the FME
questions.trap: Don't treat fit & proper as a one-time registration check — the phrase is 'at all times'.
questions.tip: Own it as your responsibility. For a PO role, showing you take personal accountability matters as much as the rule.

questions.q: Why do regulators worry about round-tripping in IFSC fund structures?
questions.answer: Because an IFSC unit is treated as non-resident for many exchange-control purposes, which is what makes offshore-in-onshore structures work. The concern is that this treatment could be misused — Indian capital leaving the country and coming back dressed as foreign investment to get a benefit it shouldn't. So when you structure a fund, you want the flows to be genuine and well-documented, and you watch for arrangements that look like capital simply doing a round trip.
questions.trap: Don't overstate specifics — if you're not sure of an exact FEMA provision, explain the principle rather than inventing a rule.
questions.tip: This is a principle question — lead with why the structure exists, then name the risk.
questions.verifyNote: FEMA detail — verify against FEMA / current notifications.

questions.q: An onboarding file is missing beneficial-ownership information. Can the investor be onboarded?
questions.answer: Not until the beneficial ownership is established. CDD requires you to identify the natural persons who ultimately own or control the investor, and that has to be done before the relationship proceeds. So I'd hold onboarding, go back for the missing information, and only clear the file once BO is verified. It's a hard gate, not a formality you complete later.
remember: Hard gate, not a later step
questions.trap: Don't say 'onboard now, collect later' — that's exactly the control failure enforcement actions flag.
questions.tip: Frame BO verification as a gate. That single word signals you understand controls.
questions.verifyNote: AML detail — verify against PML Rules.

questions.q: How would you describe the reporting obligations of an FME?
questions.answer: I'd split them into two buckets. Periodic reporting runs on a fixed cycle — regular investor and regulatory reporting; for some services that's quarterly, within a month of quarter end. Event-based reporting is triggered by a specific event, like a change in a KMP or a material change to a scheme. Running both well is basically a compliance calendar — knowing what's due, when, and what triggers a filing.
questions.trap: Don't list random filings — the interviewer wants the structure, not a memory dump.
questions.tip: The two-bucket structure is the whole answer. Give one concrete example of each.

scenarios.setup: You are the Compliance Officer of an FME. The business team wants to proceed with a transaction, but you identify a possible regulatory issue.
steps: Establish the facts — what exactly is proposed, amounts, counterparties.
Identify the applicable regulation or limit that's in play.
Assess the issue — how real and how serious is the risk?
Escalate to the Principal Officer where the decision is significant.
Document the analysis and the decision.
Take the required action — proceed compliantly, restructure, or stop.
scenarios.considerations: The mistake candidates make is jumping to a verdict before establishing facts. Facts first, always.

scenarios.setup: You are the Compliance Officer. An investor onboarding file has incomplete beneficial-ownership information.
steps: Establish what's missing — which BO details, and why.
Recognise the obligation — BO must be verified before onboarding.
Hold the file — onboarding doesn't proceed on a gap.
Request the missing information from the investor / introducer.
Verify beneficial ownership to the natural persons in control.
Only then clear the file, and document the resolution.
scenarios.considerations: Treat BO verification as a hard gate. 'Onboard now, verify later' is the exact failure pattern regulators cite.
scenarios.verifyNote: AML specifics — verify against PML Rules.

scenarios.setup: You are in Legal & Compliance. The fund team wants to launch a restricted scheme quickly and asks whether the PPM disclosures can be 'tidied up later'.
steps: Establish the timeline pressure and what's actually incomplete.
Identify the obligation — the PPM is the investor's primary disclosure.
Assess the risk — thin disclosure is a live regulatory and litigation exposure.
Push back constructively — disclosure is finalised before filing, not after.
Escalate to the PO if the business insists on cutting corners.
remember: The PPM is disclosure, not a formality
scenarios.considerations: For an L&C role, interviewers want to see you protect disclosure quality under commercial pressure.

simulations.title: The incomplete onboarding file
simulations.setup: You are the Compliance Officer. An investor onboarding file reaches you with incomplete beneficial-ownership information, and the relationship manager is keen to close this week.
simulations.obligation: CDD requires beneficial ownership to be identified and verified before the relationship proceeds.
simulations.action: Hold onboarding, request the missing BO information, verify to the ultimate natural persons, then clear and document.
simulations.mistake: Onboarding first and 'verifying later' to meet the RM's deadline.
simulations.verifyNote: AML specifics — verify against PML Rules.

simulations.title: A KMP resigns
simulations.setup: You are the Principal Officer. Your Compliance Officer — the firm's only Compliance Officer KMP — resigns with immediate effect.
simulations.obligation: A Registered FME must have a Compliance Officer KMP; changes to KMPs must follow the manner specified by IFSCA.
simulations.action: Assess the gap, arrange interim cover for the compliance function, begin identifying an eligible replacement, and notify/file the KMP change as required.
simulations.mistake: Leaving the Compliance Officer seat empty while continuing regulated activity as if nothing changed.

control.action: Interim cover + eligible replacement + KMP-change filing

controls.title: Investor onboarding — BO gate
controls.obligation: Beneficial ownership identified & verified before onboarding
controls.action: Run CDD; look through to ultimate natural persons; apply EDD if higher-risk

controls.title: KMP change control
controls.trigger: A KMP is appointed or resigns
controls.obligation: Maintain the KMP structure required for the FME category
controls.action: Confirm eligibility of replacement; arrange interim cover; file the change
controls.timeline: In the manner and time specified by IFSCA

controls.title: Periodic valuation control
controls.obligation: Value scheme assets per prescribed norms and report on time
controls.action: Obtain valuation from independent valuer; check independence & timeliness
controls.timeline: Within the prescribed window (e.g. half-yearly report within one month)
controls.filing: Valuation report retained / shared with investors
controls.monitoring: Calendar reminder; report not stale when relied on

definitions.def: Fund Management Entity — the licensed fund manager in IFSC. Three categories.
VCS or single-family investment fund; private placement to accredited investors.
Retail schemes for the public; public REIT/InvIT; ETFs.
Placement memorandum — private-placement disclosure document for accredited investors.
Public disclosure document used by a Registered FME (Retail).
KMP responsible for the overall activities of the FME.
KMP responsible for compliance + risk implementation (mandatory for Registered FME).
Continuing 'at all times' standard for FME, directors, KMPs, controlling shareholders.

timelines.v: Quarterly, within 1 month of quarter end

distinctions.note: Overall FME activities vs reporting to FIU-IND. Can be different people.
Overall activities vs compliance + risk. CO mandatory for Registered FME.
Private placement / accredited vs public / retail.
Licence vs the product that sits under it.

traps: Calling FME categories 'AIF categories' (that's SEBI/domestic language).
Assuming every FME needs a Compliance Officer — depends on category.
Treating fit & proper as a one-time check — it's 'at all times'.
Saying the PPM is 'approved' — for private schemes it's 'taken on record'.
Collapsing the FME PO and the PMLA PO into one role.

modes.label: Final 10 Minutes
modes.desc: Traps + the numbers most likely to be asked.

assessment.q: How many categories of FME are there under the IFSCA Fund Management Regulations?
assessment.explain: Three: Authorised FME, Registered FME (Non-Retail), Registered FME (Retail).

assessment.q: Which category can launch ETFs and run public retail schemes?
assessment.explain: Only the Registered FME (Retail) can run retail schemes and ETFs.

assessment.q: Minimum net worth for a Registered FME (Retail)?
assessment.explain: USD 1,000,000 — the highest of the three, matching the retail category.

assessment.q: Every FME must appoint a separate Compliance Officer.
assessment.explain: False. The Compliance Officer is mandatory for a Registered FME; an Authorised FME may run on the Principal Officer alone.

assessment.q: The Principal Officer of an FME is responsible for…
options: The overall activities of the FME
assessment.explain: The overall activities of the FME — fund management, risk and compliance.

assessment.q: Fit & proper is only tested at the time of registration.
assessment.explain: False. It is a continuing 'at all times' obligation.

assessment.q: A placement memorandum (PPM) is used to invite…
assessment.explain: The PPM is the private-placement document for accredited investors; the offer document is the public/retail one.

assessment.q: The FME Principal Officer and the PMLA Principal Officer are always the same person.
assessment.explain: False. They are different roles and can be different people. (Verify AML detail against PMLA.)

assessment.q: An onboarding file lacks beneficial-ownership information. The correct action is to…
options: Hold onboarding until BO is verified
Escalate to the business team to decide
assessment.explain: Hold onboarding — BO verification is a gate before the relationship proceeds. (Verify against PML Rules.)

assessment.q: Minimum investment for an investor in a restricted scheme (non-accredited)?
assessment.explain: USD 150,000 for a restricted scheme; accredited investors have no minimum ticket.

assessment.q: Reporting obligations are best described as…
assessment.explain: Two buckets — periodic (fixed cycle) and event-based (triggered by a change).

assessment.q: An FME can change its category whenever it wants, without approval.
assessment.explain: False. A category change needs prior approval from IFSCA.

assessment.q: The VCS total corpus is capped at…
assessment.explain: USD 200 million.

assessment.q: Accredited investors are subject to the USD 150,000 minimum ticket.
assessment.explain: False — accredited investors have no minimum ticket.

assessment.q: Additional fund-management KMP is triggered at AUM of…
assessment.explain: USD 1 billion excluding fund-of-funds AUM.

assessment.q: For a professionally-qualified Compliance Officer, minimum experience is…
assessment.explain: Three years.

assessment.q: A restricted-scheme PPM is 'approved' by IFSCA in the retail sense.
assessment.explain: False — it is 'taken on record' for private schemes.

assessment.q: The Designated Director under PMLA is…
assessment.explain: Senior AML responsibility for the reporting entity.

assessment.q: A change in KMP is which type of reporting?
assessment.explain: Event-based (triggered).

assessment.q: Which can undertake Portfolio Management Services?
assessment.explain: Registered FME (Non-Retail) can do PMS (and Retail, as a superset).

t_categories.q: How many FME categories exist under the IFSCA Fund Management Regulations?
Which category may launch ETFs and public retail schemes?
A Single Family Investment Fund is run by which category?
t_categories.explain: The Authorised FME covers VCS and single-family investment funds.

t_categories.q: Can an FME change its category on its own?
t_categories.explain: A category change requires prior approval from IFSCA.

t_categories.q: Which statement is true about the category hierarchy?
options: Retail can do everything the lower two can
t_categories.explain: Each higher category is a superset of the lower ones.

t_networth.q: Minimum net worth for an Authorised FME?
Minimum net worth for a Registered FME (Non-Retail)?
Minimum net worth for a Registered FME (Retail)?

t_networth.explain: It is a continuing 'at all times' requirement.

options: Must be separate in IFSC only
May be maintained at parent level
t_networth.explain: It may be maintained at the parent level, with the parent ensuring branch operating funds.

t_kmp.explain: A Principal Officer is mandatory for every FME.

t_kmp.q: A Compliance Officer KMP is mandatory for…
t_kmp.explain: A Registered FME must appoint a Compliance Officer.

t_kmp.q: The additional fund-management KMP is triggered at AUM of…
t_kmp.explain: AUM of at least USD 1 billion, excluding fund-of-funds AUM.

t_kmp.q: KMPs of an FME must be based…
t_kmp.explain: They must be based out of the IFSC.

t_kmp.q: A Registered FME (Retail) must add a fund-management KMP…
options: Before its first retail scheme/ETF offer document
t_kmp.explain: Before filing the offer document of its first retail scheme or ETF.

t_thresholds.q: Minimum ticket for a non-accredited investor in a restricted scheme?
Maximum number of investors in a restricted scheme?
Minimum corpus for a Venture Capital Scheme?

t_thresholds.explain: The VCS total corpus cannot exceed USD 200 million.

t_thresholds.q: For an accredited investor, the minimum ticket…
t_thresholds.explain: Accredited investors are exempt from the minimum-ticket floor.

t_po_role.q: The Principal Officer is responsible for…
options: The overall activities of the FME
t_po_role.explain: Overall activities — fund management, risk and compliance.

t_po_role.q: Which is NOT part of the PO's stated remit?
t_po_role.explain: The remit is fund management, risk and compliance.
In the IFSC, like the other KMPs.

t_po_role.q: Best framing of the PO role in an interview?
options: Ownership of the firm's regulatory posture
t_po_role.explain: It's senior ownership of the FME's regulatory posture.

t_kmp_eligibility.q: Base experience requirement for a KMP?
t_kmp_eligibility.explain: At least five years of related experience in an eligible institution.

t_kmp_eligibility.q: A PO with 15 years' fund-management experience may qualify on…
options: A graduate degree in any field
t_kmp_eligibility.explain: A graduate degree in any field suffices in that case.

t_kmp_eligibility.q: For a Compliance Officer who is professionally qualified, experience drops to…
t_kmp_eligibility.explain: Three years where the CO holds a professional qualification.

t_kmp_eligibility.q: Which additionally counts as a professional qualification for the CO specifically?
t_kmp_eligibility.explain: For the CO, an LLB also counts (alongside CA/CS/CMA).

t_kmp_eligibility.q: The KMP experience clause was most recently…
t_kmp_eligibility.explain: Substituted by the 2026 amendment — cite it as current.

t_po_vs_co.q: The Compliance Officer is specifically responsible for…
t_po_vs_co.explain: Compliance with the regulations and implementing risk-management policies.

options: May run on the PO alone
t_po_vs_co.explain: It may operate without a separate Compliance Officer.

t_po_vs_co.q: The right answer to 'must every FME have a CO?' is…
t_po_vs_co.explain: It depends on the FME category.

t_ppm_vs_offer.q: An offer document is used by…
t_ppm_vs_offer.explain: A Registered FME (Retail) inviting the public.

t_ppm_vs_offer.q: The PPM is best described as…
t_ppm_vs_offer.explain: It's the investor's primary disclosure document.
'Prospectus' is public/retail language; the PPM is a private-placement document.

t_pmla_po.q: The PMLA Principal Officer is responsible for…
t_pmla_po.explain: Reporting to FIU-IND under the PMLA framework.

t_pmla_po.q: The FME Principal Officer and PMLA Principal Officer are…
options: Different roles that can be different people
The same title only for retail
t_pmla_po.explain: Different roles; they can be different individuals.

t_pmla_po.q: Senior AML responsibility under PMLA sits with the…
t_pmla_po.explain: The Designated Director carries senior AML responsibility.

t_valuation_custodian.q: An FME must appoint an independent…
t_valuation_custodian.explain: An independent custodian, generally based in IFSC.

t_valuation_custodian.q: For a Compliance Officer, the key valuation points are…
t_valuation_custodian.explain: Independence of the valuer and timeliness of reports.

t_reporting.q: A change in KMP is an example of…
t_reporting.explain: It's triggered by a specific event.

options: Quarterly, within a month of quarter end
t_reporting.explain: Quarterly, within one month of quarter end.
